$comment: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for subscription tiers.
Prices appear in at least four places that must agree: the entitlement
checks in the API, the pricing page, the App Store / Play Console product
definitions, and the docs. Four copies of a number is four chances to
drift, and the one that drifts silently is the entitlement check -- a
customer charged for Family whose device cap still says Pro. So the number
lives here once and every surface reads it.
Reasoning and the decisions behind these values: docs/PRICING.md
Validated by tests/test_pricing_is_coherent.py
14, not 7. This product proves itself when it BLOCKS something, which
is an event that may not happen in a light user's first week. A trial
that ends before the product has had a chance to demonstrate value
converts on faith rather than evidence.
reminder_days_before_charge is not optional politeness. Auto-renewal
after a trial is regulated (FTC negative-option / click-to-cancel, EU
consumer law, and both app stores), and several jurisdictions require
advance notice. It is also the conversion moment: the reminder carries
the 'here is what we caught for you' summary, so the compliance step
and the sales step are the same message.
3 devices, not 1. Remember one-device-many-surfaces: a laptop running
the extension and the agent is ONE device, so a 1-device tier means
phone OR laptop, not both. With no free tier this is the acquisition
point, and it must not feel broken at the moment of first payment.
Phone + laptop + tablet is what a normal person owns.
10 devices, not 5. Devices cost well under a cent per month in
compute (measured: ~0.89s/scan on the consumer profile, plus the
content-hash cache), so generosity here is nearly free and it removes
the reason anyone would want a per-device add-on.
7 people, not 6. This was 6 to match Apple Family Sharing, on the
reasoning that the mental model is already installed and fighting it
buys nothing. That was the wrong read. Apple, Microsoft 365 Family and
Google One ALL stop at 6, so 6 is not a neutral default -- it is the
number at which a household discovers it does not fit, and every
competitor fails them at the same place.
Two parents and five children is an ordinary family. So is one with a
grandparent living in it. Exceeding the installed model by exactly one
is legible BECAUSE that model is installed: 'the one that fits our
family' is a claim a customer verifies in five seconds against the
plan they already pay for. We are not fighting the anchor, we are
using it.
The 7th seat costs us nothing that 6 did not -- devices are the
compute cost and the device cap did not move.
30 devices is effectively unlimited for a household, which is a
simplicity win: nobody has to administer quotas inside their own home.
The 7-person limit is the real constraint against sharing.

$comment_addon: DELIBERATELY NULL, and it should stay null.
A $34 per-additional-device add-on was proposed and rejected 2026-08-16:
* The marginal rate exceeded the average rate. Pro at $79.99 for 10
devices is $8/device/year; a $34 add-on is four times that. Marginal
price should decline with volume, not multiply.
* There is no cost basis. Compute per device is under a cent a month.
* It is an SMB mental model. Consumers ask 'does this cover my stuff',
not 'how many seats do I need'. Norton, Bitdefender and McAfee all
* It charges friction at the worst possible moment. Someone adding a
6th device is the most engaged user you have -- the one most likely
to renew and refer. Teaching them that adoption costs extra is
Someone who outgrows a tier upgrades to the next one. That is a bigger,
cleaner sale with no billing surprise.

$comment: Modelled, not ignored. Apple and Google take 15% under $1M/yr (Small
Business Program) and 30% above it. On Family annual that is $18 or $36
off the top. Stripe on web is ~2.9% + 30c.
Prices are deliberately IDENTICAL on every channel at launch. A
web-direct discount is real money but it adds a second price to
explain, per-jurisdiction anti-steering rules to track, and a support
burden -- for a saving that is not material until revenue is. Revisit
when the fee is a number worth optimising.
